addresses: visual-phone, major: 'the remedy came up out of the basement and stopped exactly on the sticky tab bar... the re-check reports into nowhere... the bottom 55% of both buttons overlaps the navigation bar'
visual-phone, major, direction: 'verdict, explanation, then the two buttons and their reply, then the pre'
changes.change: The order inside 'This deployment' is now verdict, explanation, [Copy command | Check again] and the aria-live reply, then the gcloud block, then the identifying facts. The pre came out of the action group and became its own sibling at the section's 12px gap; the group that remains is the two buttons and the line that answers them. Measured at 390x844: the buttons are y=634-678 and the reply y=686-706, both entirely clear of the tab bar's top edge at 776, and the pre starts at 718 and is allowed to run under the bar.
changes.rationale: I agree with the reading and took it whole. The command is the only object in the block that is read once and copied — it is reference you scroll to, and nothing about it is aimed at; the button that must be pressed again in ninety seconds and the sentence that says 'still no' are the two things that cannot be under opaque chrome. Putting 'Copy command' above the command it copies is the only cost, and a button that names its object does not need to sit beneath it. At lg the same order reads as cause, remedy, controls, evidence, identifiers — the explanation ends 'Grant it, then check again', and 'Check again' is now the next thing under it rather than 90px below a code block, so the desktop reading is better for the same reason the phone one is.
changes.breakpoint: both — one order, no breakpoint. The tab bar only exists below lg, but the order is right at both widths.
changes.implementation: KioskPage.tsx SigningCard: move the `<pre>` out of the `flex flex-col gap-2` actions wrapper and render it after that wrapper, still inside the section's `flex flex-col gap-3`. Final child order in the section: h2, verdict+explanation group, actions group (button row + aria-live reply), pre, dl.

addresses: visual-desktop, major: "'If the kiosk still waits' was placed inside the core-team region, so the person the journey says is actually standing there never sees it... none of these three lines is a call — they are static prose"
design-phone, minor: 'the counselor page fits the viewport with room to spare and then trails off... a fifth of the frame is empty'
changes.change: 'If the kiosk still waits' left the core-gated region and now renders for every active member. On the counselor's page it appears under its own rule, after the pairing form and the '✓ Check in' exit and before the footer rule — same heading style, same 12px ink-400 body, same three items. Its third item made the counselor's retirement paragraph redundant, so that paragraph was trimmed to match the admin's ('To retire a kiosk, clear the browser's site data…'); the fact moved, it is not stated twice. On the core pages nothing moved on screen: the section still sits at the head of the right-hand column above Phone search. The counselor's phone page now runs 903px instead of 665px, so the empty fifth is gone and the last thing that scrolls off is the small print rather than nothing.
changes.rationale: Sharpest finding of the round and I agree with it without reservation. The constraint is 'a counselor must not be shown a call that will be refused' — these three lines are not a call, they are prose the app already ships, they mention no project configuration and they claim nothing about the lobby screen's health. Two of the three are her exact failure modes: the code went stale while she walked back to the iPad, and the iPad has Tally installed to its home screen so it keeps its own storage and asks a second time. Without them her next move is to phone an admin, which the journey calls the end of the journey. I kept the exit above the section rather than moving it to the foot — design-phone's other option — because the page is now 903px tall and the counselor's only route onward would have landed below the fold; at y=415 it stays in the thumb band and the two reference registers descend in rank beneath it.
changes.breakpoint: both. Below lg it is a stacked section on every build; at lg it is column two of the core register and a full-measure section on the counselor's 672px column.

KioskPage.tsx: StuckKioskCard stops being inside the `core &&` branch. One region, gated per child — `

What is still core-gated after this: SigningCard only (the verdict, the explanation, the gcloud command, Copy command / Check again, the re-check reply, and the Project / Service account identifiers) plus PhoneIndexCard. Everything else on the page — lede, form, hint, 'If the kiosk still waits', both footer paragraphs — renders for any active member.

addresses: visual-desktop, minor: 'a page whose left column already names the single cause in force offers, on its right, three causes that are all false right now... noise placed under a heading that promises to be the answer'
changes.change: Taken, in the sequencing form rather than the withholding form. When the deployment cannot sign tokens, the section leads with one ink-500 line above the list: 'Once the role is granted, these are the remaining reasons a kiosk keeps waiting.' The three items are unchanged and the healthy page is unchanged.
changes.rationale: Withholding was the other option and I rejected it: the section is now ungated and its job is to be there when a kiosk waits, so making it disappear in the state where somebody is most likely to be reading the page is the wrong instinct. One subordinating sentence at the register's lowest contrast does the whole job — it says these are not the cause in force, and it keeps the list available for the second failure, which on a denied deployment is exactly what happens after the grant propagates. Nothing new is claimed and no accent enters.

KioskPage.tsx StuckKioskCard takes an `ok` prop from the same status query the SigningCard reads; when `ok === false` it renders `

addresses: design-desktop, minor: 'the register is declared as three columns and drawn as two with a hole in the middle... the two peer sections then set their bodies at two different measures, ~80 characters on the left and ~58 on the right'
changes.change: The register's grid changed from `lg:grid-cols-3` with a `lg:col-span-2` deployment block to two explicit columns at 3:2 — 672px and 448px with the same 32px gutter. The empty band inside the deployment column falls from 293px to 176px and the two bodies now wrap at 496px and 448px, close enough to read as peers.
changes.rationale: Of the critic's two options — put the block in one column, or spend the width it has — neither was available whole: a single 363px column cannot hold the three-line gcloud command without wrapping identifiers again, which was r02's fix; and laying the identifiers across the width would undo the 'facts come last, as the tail of the block' ordering the same critic asked for in r02. 3:2 is the resolution: the block keeps the width the command actually needs, the reference column grows 85px, and the measures converge without moving a single element. The 'diagonal of void' shrinks to ordinary trailing space in a column whose widest object is a code block.
changes.breakpoint: lg and up only. Below lg the region is `flex flex-col gap-6` and nothing about it changes.
changes.implementation: KioskPage.tsx: the region's class becomes `… lg:grid lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,3fr)_minmax(0,2fr)] lg:items-start lg:gap-8`, and SigningCard's section loses `lg:col-span-2`.

addresses: design-phone, minor: 'the panel's ring begins 3px from the viewport edge, against the 16px inset every other block shares — neither aligned nor bled'
design-desktop, minor: 'the command block is 290px wider than the longest line inside it... its right edge reaches into the column gutter and stops 20px short of an unrelated column's text'
changes.change: Two edges, one element. The outdent is now `lg:-mx-3`: below lg the panel sits on the page column with the h1, the field and every heading, and above lg it keeps the 12px hang into a 32px gutter that puts its first character on the page's left edge. And the panel is `w-fit`, so it stops at the width its own lines need — 506px at 1440 instead of 781px — which leaves a 210px gutter to 'If the kiosk still waits' and stops the block looking half empty. On the phone `w-fit` resolves to the full column, because the command is wider than 358px however it is set.
changes.rationale: The 3px margin was the hang being sized to the desktop's gutter and applied to the phone's; a hang has to be smaller than the gutter it hangs into or it reads as a slip, and at 16px of page padding there is no gutter to hang into. Sizing the panel to its content is the same idea on the other edge: a code block is as wide as its longest line, not as wide as the column it happens to sit in, and once it is, the one place two registers meet has more air than anything else on the page rather than less.
changes.breakpoint: the outdent is lg and up; the width is unconditional and simply resolves differently at 358px.
changes.implementation: KioskPage.tsx: the `pre` class becomes `w-fit select-text whitespace-pre-wrap break-words rounded-lg bg-ink-900 px-3 py-2 font-mono text-xs leading-relaxed text-ink-200 ring-1 ring-ink-800 lg:-mx-3`.

addresses: design-phone, minor: 'the reply slot reserves more height than its line uses, and the surplus falls out of the bottom of the group... two gaps the eye cannot tell apart, one of them internal'
visual-desktop, minor: 'a fair share of consecutive clicks land inside the same displayed minute and render a byte-identical string'
changes.change: The reply reserves one line instead of two (`min-h-8` → `min-h-5`, one 12px/leading-relaxed line), which takes the surplus out of the group's bottom edge: on the phone the gap from the reply to the fact list is now 12px against 24px between sections, so the identifiers read as the tail of the block whose heading they sit under. Two lines were over-reserved anyway — the longest reply string, 'Cannot sign kiosk tokens — checked just now', is 43 characters and sets on one line at 358px. And the time went relative: 'Checked 2 min ago' rather than 'Checked 6:41 pm'.
changes.rationale: The two findings are the same element and pull the same way once the reserve is measured rather than assumed. On the resolution point: a relative phrase alone does not close it — two clicks thirty seconds apart both say 'just now' — so the click gets a visible beginning as well as an end. 'Check again' disables and reads 'Checking…' while the call is in flight, and the reply resets to 'just now' from whatever it had decayed to. Between them, no press can look like nothing happened. The clock time is not lost, it moves to the element's `title`, because `checkedAt` is the client's own record and a relative phrase is the honest register for it.
changes.implementation:
KioskPage.tsx SigningCard: `

`, text from a relative formatter (`Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`, or the same helper the roster uses) over the client's `checkedAt`. The re-check button takes `disabled={isFetching}` and `{isFetching ? 'Checking…' : 'Check again'}`.

addresses: design-phone, minor: 'six 3px dots sit in the middle of a 358x60 surface... the object that arrives at a squint is a large empty tray rather than six waiting slots'
design-phone, minor: 'its centre also sits about 3px left of the box's centre, because the trailing letter-space of the tracking is being counted into the centring'
changes.change: The placeholder is six bullets (U+2022) instead of six middle dots, so each mark is about 9px at the field's 30px monospace rather than 3px, and the resting field shows six slots at the weight of the glyphs that will land in them. The trailing letter-space is taken out of the centring with `indent-[0.2em]`, which offsets the centred line by exactly half the 0.2em trailing space — correct for the typed value as well as the placeholder.
changes.rationale: The cheapest possible answer to 'correct in rank, mute in content': no new element, no marked-up slots, one character swapped and one offset. Six discrete marks at the size of the answer is the field saying 'six characters' without being read, which is the one thing it could not say. Marked positions drawn by the surface would be a new visual language for a single control, so I did not.
changes.breakpoint: both — the field is the same object at 358px and at 7em.
changes.implementation: src/components/ui/Field.tsx, the `code` preset: `placeholder="••••••"` and add `indent-[0.2em]` beside `tracking-[0.2em]`.

addresses: design-phone, minor: 'the identity block is twice the height of the list, carries four text objects to the list's one, and holds the panel's only chroma... in a navigation surface the destinations should arrive before the account'
design-desktop, minor: 'the destination is set at exactly the lightness already spent on the email address... a navigation surface whose loudest element is the way out'
visual-phone, minor: 'in the right-hand 74px of that strip — precisely where a right thumb travels — is Sign out'
changes.change: Three small moves in one block. The 'Signed in as' caption is gone, so the identity is two lines instead of three and the block falls from 99px to 72px against a 48px row. The email steps down the ramp (ink-200 → ink-400) and the destination rows step up (ink-200 → ink-100), so the first thing the panel presents is where you can go. And 'Sign out' moved off the thumb's column: it now sits immediately after the role chip on the left (`justify-between gap-3` → `gap-2`, `-mr-2` → `-ml-2`), keeping its 44px box and its danger colour, so the right-hand 74px above the bottom-most row is inert text.
changes.rationale: One panel, three critics, one cause: with a counselor's single destination the header outweighed the list, and the only coloured object in it sat exactly where a thumb reaching the bottom row undershoots. Lowering the identity and raising the destinations fixes the rank without touching the exit's colour — which r02 already quietened once and which should not be quietened twice, or it stops being findable on purpose. Dropping the caption is what pays for the proportion: the chip you tapped names the person, so an email under it needs no label. On the admin build the same edit is right and invisible — three white rows against a dimmer account block.
changes.breakpoint: both — the sheet below lg and the popover at lg are the same item list in two containers, as before.
changes.implementation: AppShell.tsx, the shared account-menu identity block: delete the `Signed in as` paragraph; email becomes `truncate text-xs text-ink-400`; the row becomes `mt-1 flex items-center gap-2` with the sign-out button at `-ml-2 flex min-h-11 items-center rounded-lg px-2 text-sm font-medium text-danger-400 hover:bg-ink-800 pointer-fine:min-h-8`; every menu destination link moves `text-ink-200` → `text-ink-100`.

declined.finding: design-phone, minor: 'either the reference paragraphs move above the exit so the action is the last thing the composition offers, or the exit takes the foot of the frame'.
declined.why: Half-taken, and I am declining the half that names the order. The emptiness is gone — the counselor's page went from 665px of content in an 844px frame to 903px — but the exit stayed above the two reference registers rather than moving to the foot. On the taller page the foot is y≈860, which would put this role's only route onward below the fold on the one screen the journey says she is holding in one hand at 6:40pm. Reach beats closure here; the page now descends in rank, job → way onward → troubleshooting → small print, which is a composition rather than a trailing off.

declined.finding: design-desktop, minor: 'either the deployment block sits in one column like its peers and the register reads as three equal columns of reference, or the two-column allowance is actually used — the identifying facts and the re-check reply laid across the width'.
declined.why: Neither option taken literally; 3:2 taken instead, and the reasoning is in the change above. One column of 363px re-breaks the gcloud identifiers that r02 spent a change unwrapping, and spreading the facts across the width contradicts the 'facts are the tail of the block' order this same critic asked for last round. The measured outcome — 176px of trailing space, bodies at 496px and 448px — is what the finding was actually about.

declined.finding: visual-desktop, minor (residue): the reply is still only reliable because of a pending state that no frozen frame can show.
declined.why: Noted rather than declined. The prototype is a resting page, so 'Checking…' on a disabled button and the reply's reset to 'just now' exist only in the spec line above. Everything renderable about the finding — the relative phrasing, the reserved single line — is in the frames; the transient is one prop on the button and cannot be photographed here.

declined.finding: design-phone, minor (residue): the counselor's page now scrolls by 59px.
declined.why: Accepted as the price of the desktop major. The 59px is the last line of the retirement footnote, which is the lowest-ranked prose on the page and the one thing on it that is meant to scroll away. The alternative was to leave a counselor with no answer to 'the iPad is still asking to be paired', which is the finding that outranks it.
